episode_title: Episode 37: Rediscovering Creativity & Building A Design Business

real_qa.q: Why did Jo Calver split Isla James Interiors and Isla James Lighting into two separate companies?
real_qa.r: Jo wanted the lighting division to operate independently so other interior designers and architects could approach them without conflict of interest, since the services were previously integrated. She also recognized that international clients perceive London as the design hub, making a London-based address critical for the lighting business to compete globally, whereas the interior design studio could operate successfully from Berkshire.
real_qa.requete: Isla James Interiors Isla James Lighting separate companies

real_qa.q: What was Jo Calver's approach to hiring her first employee and what did she recommend about experience level?
real_qa.r: Jo saved a full year's salary before taking on her first hire to feel secure about the commitment. She hired Sophie, a mid-weight designer with six and a half years of experience, rather than a junior, because experienced hires add immediate value, hit the ground running, and earn their salary in month one—avoiding the years of training and risk that come with junior staff.
real_qa.requete: first employee hire experience level salary savings

real_qa.q: How does Jo Calver organize her interior design team into pods and manage project capacity?
real_qa.r: Jo organizes her 11-person team into three pods, each consisting of a senior designer, a mid-weight, and a junior designer assigned to roughly three major projects. She uses CMAP, an architectural project management system, to track all staff availability, holidays, invoicing, and time allocation across projects, allowing her to see exactly who can take on new work at any moment.
real_qa.requete: design team pods project management CMAP

real_qa.q: What was Jo Calver's experience transitioning from the NHS to entrepreneurship and what triggered her departure?
real_qa.r: Jo worked as a paediatric nurse at John Radcliffe Hospital in Oxford for three months in the trauma unit and enjoyed the work but not the NHS culture. She left after being told she had to bring her own pen to work, which she felt symbolized a lack of care for staff. She then spent four years in pharmaceutical sales before eventually starting Isla James Interiors in 2015.
real_qa.requete: Jo Calver NHS nurse biro pen story

real_qa.q: How long did Jo Calver work solo before expanding her design team at Isla James Interiors?
real_qa.r: Jo worked alone for the first five years after founding Isla James Interiors in November 2015, until 2020. She describes the decision to hire her first employee as the biggest step she has ever taken in business, as it marked the moment she became responsible for someone else's salary and livelihood.
real_qa.requete: Isla James Interiors five years solo before first hire

guest.bio_context: Jo Calver trained as a paediatric nurse and worked in the NHS before transitioning to pharmaceutical sales for four years. She began designing homes for friends while raising her children and completed the KLC interior design course when her husband's company relocated to Germany. She founded Isla James Interiors in November 2015 and worked solo for five years before expanding to 11 full-time staff across a design studio in Berkshire and a lighting studio in London.
